description: Bovine coronavirus (BCoV) causes diarrhea in calves, winter dysentery in adult cattle, and respiratory diseases, posing a significant threat to the cattle industry. In this study, a BCoV strain was isolated from intestinal lymph node tissues of infected calves in Hami, Xinjiang, using HRT-18G cells with an optimized trypsin-HEPES synergistic culture system. Following plaque purification, the virus was confirmed by RT-PCR, indirect immunofluorescence assay, and transmission electron microscopy, and designated as BCoV-XJHM. The viral titer reached 10 8.0  TCID 50 /mL. Whole-genome sequencing revealed that BCoV-XJHM shares 98.4–99.2% nucleotide identity with 35 representative domestic strains, clustering with the Guangxi strain (GX-NN230328, PP599028.1) in the same evolutionary subclade. Two amino acid substitutions (S81A and S149A) were observed in the N-terminal domain of the nucleocapsid (N) protein.
